newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Fed watching, EDP to drive Lisbon stocks.
newsitem.headline: Fed watching, EDP to drive Lisbon stocks.

text.p: U.S. interest rate concerns, continuing uncertainty around European monetary union and privatisation of utility giant EDP-Electricidade de Portugal would drive Lisbon stocks over the next quarter, analysts said on Monday.

Possible higher U.S. interest rates remained the central focus of investors, who had already discounted a 25 basis point hike by the U.S. Federal Reserve on Tuesday. Uncertainty would persist even if the decision was to hold rates.
"If (Fed Chairman Alan) Greenspan raises rates as expected, the Lisbon market will take it in its stride and push on upwards," said Jose Freire of ESR-Espirito Santo Research.
Over the past week, expectations of an imminent U.S. rate rise had braked the powerful advance of Portuguese stocks this year, dealers said.
The PSI20 index of 20 leading stocks has gained 16 percent since the end of 1996. The Ibex 35 index of Spanish stocks has risen some four percent over the same period.

The Portuguese shares that were most vulnerable to external events include Portugal Telecom and Banco Comercial Portugues, both liquid stocks traded on the New York stock exchange and popular with foreign investors.
Nagging doubts about an on-time launch of the Euro in 1999 could also drag on shares over the coming months, analysts said.

As uncertainty over the future single currency rose recently, the spread between Portuguese bonds and German Bunds -- a measure of the added risk of holding Portugal's debt -- ballooned from historic lows of 80 basis points at the end of January to the present level of 104. A basis point is one hundredth of a percentage point.
"Spreads have widened, but the outlook for corporate earnings remains good," said James Harrison of Lisbon broker Midas.
Freire said investors could be tempted to take profits after many Portuguese companies pay out dividends in April.

'Blue chip' stocks had also suffered as some investors sold them to raise cash to buy shares in the May privatisation of up to 49 percent of EDP, Portugal's dominant producer and distributor of electricity, analyst Juan Simon of Banco Efisa said.
The offering was expected to boost turnover on the Lisbon bourse by between 15 and 20 percent, ESR-Espirito Santo Research said in a report earlier this month.
EDP, with a capital of 600 billion escudos ($3.5 billion), will have the biggest market capitalisation on the Lisbon bourse.
Analysts expected foreign and domestic private and institutional investors to pile into the privatisation of the well-managed EDP, which they said would be comfortably oversubscribed.
"The EDP sale will help sentiment and could encourage another rally in Portuguese shares," said Simon.

Analysts said the firmest bets over the next quarter included cement and construction stocks, which were benefiting from public works projects and the 1998 Lisbon Expo World Fair, and Portugal Telecom, expected to announce an international strategic alliance soon.
When Cimpor reveals its 1996 results on Wednesday, it could announce a "surprise" special dividend resulting from the sale of a stake in privatised bank Banco de Fomento e Exterior, Harrison said.
Another area of market focus could be arbitrage between shares of wood products group Sonae Industria and Inparsa in the coming weeks, he added.
Inparsa, created from a reorganisation of the Sonae group, combines a majority stake in Sonae Industria and the media, computing and tourism businesses of Pargeste. ($1=170.105 escudos)
